sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: CONCMID-GEO-SID
TITLE: Concentration-scaled geodesic step toward each item's behaviour-successor barycentre, taken before level-1 quantization (items move, codebooks do not).
MOTIVATION: The SID is currently determined by where an item's text latent happens to sit in the ball. That geometry knows nothing about what the item is followed by, so at depth three 24,556 items are compressed into 2,201 prefixes (~11 items each) whose members are textually similar but behaviourally unrelated; Stage3 then has to spend prefix tokens discriminating items that the prefix says are the same, or predicting a next item whose prefix is not the prefix that behaviour would have chosen. Issue 126 says the recall-predictive structure is behaviour-CONTRAST (within-group tightness plus between-group separation), not Gromov-delta and not ancestor depth, so the fix has to be a partition change driven by directed behaviour contrast, not another additive loss.
NOVELTY: Different coupling position from everything already tried here. The rejected/prior mechanisms changed (a) codebook centroids via successor-weighted Frechet means, (b) per-level curvature from hard prefix-transition scores, (c) the radial coordinate by context entropy, (d) Lorentz successor-profile smoothing of the codebook, (e) a behaviour cone on prefixes, (f) a successor boost shift. This one leaves the codebooks, the loss and the encoder completely untouched and instead moves the QUANTIZER INPUT: each item is transported along the geodesic toward the tangent-mean of the items that actually follow it, by a step size equal to the measured concentration (Herfindahl) of its own popularity-adjusted transition distribution. There is no origin-minimising objective (the round-one collapse mode), because nothing is optimised: it is a deterministic, closed-form, once-per-run input transformation. No Gromov delta, no ancestor-depth weight, no tree premise. The curvature is not a scale gauge here: the operation is a basepoint-dependent exponential map at each item's own position, which has no flat counterpart at equal step size.
CHANGE: Replace the frozen per-item latent z_i that feeds the RQ chain by b_i = exp_{z_i}( eta_i * sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j) ), where w_ij are popularity-adjusted directed-transition weights computed from the Stage-2 training split only and eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2 is the measured concentration. Nothing else in Stage2 or Stage3 changes.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Geometry, fixed curvature c = 1, unit Poincare ball B = {x in R^32 : ||x|| < 1}.\n  scale: kappa = 0.9 / max_i ||t_i||  (t_i = frozen Stage-1 text latent, d = 32), computed once, so every point starts inside radius tanh(0.9) = 0.716.\n  z_i = exp_0(kappa t_i) = tanh(kappa||t_i||) * t_i/||t_i||.\n  log_z(w) = d_B(z,w) * (w (-) z)/||w (-) z||, with Moebius difference (w (-) z) = ((1-||z||^2)w - (1-2<z,w>+||w||^2)z) / (1-2<z,w>+||z||^2||w||^2) and d_B(z,w) = 2*atanh(||w (-) z||).\n  exp_z(u) = z (+) tanh(||u||) * u/||u||  (Moebius addition).\nBehaviour weights, from the Stage-2 training interaction sequences only:\n  count lag-1 pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) with weight 1.0 and lag-2 pairs (i_t, i_{t+2}) with weight 0.5, over all training sequences truncated at the Stage-2 split boundary;\n  p_ij = C_ij / sum_k C_ik ;  popularity p_j = (#occurrences of j)/(#training events);\n  adjusted  w_ij = (p_ij / p_j^{1/2}) / sum_k (p_ik / p_k^{1/2}), over {j : C_ij > 0, j != i}.\nStep: v_i = sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j) ;  eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2 ;  b_i = exp_{z_i}(eta_i v_i).\nQuantize: feed b_i into the existing curved residual chain (3 levels x 256 codewords, CODEBOOK_DIM 32) and train the codebooks exactly as the baseline does for 3000 epochs.\nSwitches (all present in code, only both-on trained): BEHAV_SMOOTH in {False,True}; CURV_C in {1.0, 0.0}; both-on = (True, 1.0). BEHAV_SMOOTH=False sets eta_i = 0 for all i, hence b_i = z_i exactly. CURV_C = 0.0 replaces every exp/log by its flat limit, i.e. z_i = kappa t_i, log_z(w) = w - z, b_i = z_i + eta_i sum_j w_ij (z_j - z_i), and the residual chain becomes a flat RQ-VAE; that is the Euclidean counterfactual, with the same weights and the same eta.'}
COST: One static precompute and zero per-step cost. Precompute: build the lag-1/lag-2 sparse count matrix from the training sequences (order 10^6 nonzeros), row-normalise, popularity-adjust, then one log map per nonzero plus one exp map per item, over d = 32: roughly 1.5e6 x ~150 flops ~ 2e8 flops, a few seconds on one GPU, and a 24,556 x 32 float32 table (3.1 MB). At the frozen scale (24,556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 4096 global batch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps) the added per-step cost is a single row-gather: 0 FLOPs, 0 added communication, no change to DDP bucket sizes. Stage2 wall clock therefore stays at the measured 571 s / 0.145 s per epoch plus about 5 s of precompute (<1%); Stage3 is untouched at 150 epochs.
HYPOTHESIS: What must be true is that (i) items with a concentrated, popularity-adjusted successor distribution are exactly the items whose text latent is a poor guide to their next-item role (serialised content, tightly coupled co-consumption), and (ii) the curved step damps far moves more than a flat blend would, because items already near the ball boundary would otherwise be pushed onto their neighbour's prefix and collapse level-1 usage. If both hold, moving those items onto the geodesic toward their successors' tangent barycentre raises prefix-level predictability (the level-3 token becomes predictable from levels 1-2 and the last item) while the boundary damping keeps the partition spread out. Observed as: level-1 active codewords stay >= 240, distinct L2/L3 prefixes stay >= 1,700, within-prefix behaviour dispersion drops, between-prefix contrast rises, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run.
RISKS: ["The concentration step may be tiny for most items (diffuse real-world transition distributions), in which case b_i ~ z_i, the SID is effectively unchanged and the run reproduces round one's 0.054; the eta histogram and the SID-change fraction are recorded for exactly this reason. Popularity adjustment with exponent 1/2 may be too weak, so many items are pulled onto the same hub and level-1/level-3 prefix counts fall. Because the geometry is frozen, the mechanism can only repartition the existing Stage-1 geometry, which round one showed yields a modest ceiling; the step is not allowed to fix a bad text geometry, only to re-aim it. Curvature may turn out to be a near-gauge for the smoothed points (the flat and curved midpoints differ only at second order for small steps), in which case the geometry contributes little; since no geometry-off arm is trained, this is recorded as an untested risk, not an admission gate. Duplicate SIDs could appear where two items share a dominant successor; a deterministic one-pass repair is specified. Finally, the whole mechanism depends on the transition matrix being informative for cold items, which it is not; those keep eta_i = 0."]
END IDEA

IDEA: behtree-geocut-sid
TITLE: Behaviour-cut geodesic prefix tree with prefix-local SID ids and hyperbolic soft-assignment (fixed gyrobarycentric anchors)
MOTIVATION: Round one produced 2201 distinct 3-token triples for 24556 items, so ~11 behaviourally different items share one SID and the generative model cannot separate them; the curvature and the prefix structure were also decoupled, and the curved reconstruction objective killed the encoder. The problem addressed is that prefix capacity and prefix membership are allocated by text-reconstruction geometry, not by what users actually do next.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds changed codebook positions (successor-weighted Frechet), per-level curvature, radial rank from entropy/context entropy, cones, per-level boosts and residuals, all on a shared RQ codebook with 256 codes per level. Here the SID is a *tree path in a behaviour-cut geodesic partition*, the token alphabet is prefix-local (the same id at level 2 means different items under different parents), and the fanout of every node is decided by a degree-preserving-null significance test on directed train transitions. So the mechanism changes *which items may share a token and how many distinct triples exist*, i.e. the prefix structure and the SID capacity allocation, not the positions inside a fixed triplet of codebooks. Geometry is not a curvature value (curvature is fixed at c=1 because it is a gauge) but the shape of the separator: geodesic hyperplanes, affine in the Klein chart, sphere arcs in the Poincare model, which cut the item set differently from any Euclidean plane in the Poincare coordinates.
CHANGE: The RQ-VAE assignment is replaced by a descent through a fixed behaviour-built hyperbolic tree: at each of three levels the encoder output competes only among its parent's children, scored by exact Poincare distance to the children's fixed gyrobarycentric anchors, and trained by hierarchical cross-entropy; the tree's fanout and leaves come from directed-train-transition cut tests on geodesic hyperplanes.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Build once from train transitions C: symmetric normalised adjacency, top-32 spectral embedding, lift to the ball as v_i = r_i * g_i/||g_i||. Recursively split each node S by (i) the Fiedler vector of the normalised behaviour Laplacian on S, (ii) the affine (Klein) bisector of the two sides' Klein centroids, (iii) re-assignment by the sign of that affine form until stable, and accept the split only if cut <= E_null[cut] - 2*sigma_null. Recurse to depth 5 per SID level (fanout <= 32) and 3 SID levels. Anchors a_c = Karcher barycentre of {v_i : i in child c}, then frozen. Encoder z = f(x), v = tanh(||z||) z/||z||; logits at level l are -d_P(v, a_c) over the children of the parent chosen at level l-1; loss = text reconstruction (straight-through) + sum_l -log softmax(-d_P). Stage3 unchanged: three tokens per item from a <=32-id-per-level alphabet inside the existing 256-token vocabulary."}
COST: Stage2 per-step is not larger than baseline: level-1 distance is 4096x32 anchors, levels 2 and 3 gather only the parent's <=32 children, i.e. 4096*3*32*32 ~ 1.3e7 multiply-adds per step versus the baseline dense 4096x256 codebook matmuls, so expect 0.145 s/epoch to become about 0.14-0.16 s/epoch, i.e. 420-480 s for 3000 epochs at 24 steps/epoch on 4096-item batches. One-off preprocessing: sparse Lanczos top-32 on a ~24.5k x 24.5k transition matrix, ~20-40 s; recursive splits and Klein-bisector iterations over at most 32k nodes, ~2-6 min; ~20 Karcher iterations over 24.5k points in 32 dims, <10 s. Total wall clock +5 to +15 percent, all of it before the first Stage2 step; Stage3 decode cost is identical because the SID length and vocabulary width are unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: The claim is that behaviourally coherent prefixes plus capacity where behaviour is heterogeneous give the Stage3 beam more usable conditional structure than a text-reconstruction partition, and that the extra effective depth (leaves up to 32^3 instead of 2201 triples) is not paid for in prediction difficulty. It is worth keeping if, in the single run, leaves per item count drops well below the round-one 14 items per deepest prefix, the prefix-conditional concentration of the training successor distribution rises (recorded, not gated), Stage2 reconstruction stays finite with no prefix-count collapse (level-1 children used >= 75 percent of allocated children at every level over the last 200 epochs), and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
RISKS: ['Prefix-local ids force one shared token embedding to serve several parent contexts, which can make Stage3 harder to learn and could lose more than the capacity gain; near-unique leaves can destroy the prefix sharing that lets TIGER generalise and may lower recall@10; the 2-sigma null test may accept too few splits on a sparse transition graph, degenerating to a shallow tree and re-creating collisions; tail items with no transitions get degenerate ball coordinates; the hierarchical CE and the text reconstruction can fight, and the straight-through path may let the encoder satisfy CE while the decoder loses text fidelity.']
END IDEA

IDEA: holonomy-frame-sid
TITLE: Behavioural-drift holonomy rotates the per-prefix code frame of the hyperbolic RQ-VAE, so where a prefix's successors drift decides which codewords its items receive.
MOTIVATION: Round one showed where the problem is flat. Level 1 already uses essentially all 256 codewords, while levels 2 and 3 produce only 1,769 and 2,201 distinct prefixes over 24,556 items (about 11 items per deepest triple). The ranking cannot move unless the PREFIX STRUCTURE moves, i.e. unless items sharing an (L1,L2,L3) triple stop sharing it. At the same time issue 126 says the radial coordinate is only group compactness and that permuting radii destroys the correlation, while Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weighting actively hurt. So the usable behaviour signal is a CONTRAST/direction signal, and the usable geometric object is not a radius but a frame. This idea takes the one curvature-specific quantity with no Euclidean analogue - the holonomy, the rotation a tangent vector picks up when parallel-transported around a closed geodesic loop - and uses it to orient the residual codebook of every prefix, driven by where that prefix's training-only successors actually go.
NOVELTY: Not a weighted assignment, not a Frechet codebook update, not a per-level curvature, not an entropy-ranked radius, not Gromov-delta weighting. Curvature is FIXED at c = 1 (gauge-fixed, exactly as issue 126(b) requires) and nothing about curvature is learned; what is measured is the AREA of a geodesic triangle (origin, prefix text anchor, prefix successor anchor), and that area becomes a holonomy rotation of the code frame in the 2-plane spanned by the two anchors' disagreement. The mechanism is provably inert (identical to the baseline assignment) when behaviour adds no directional information, and it is also inert in the Euclidean limit, so it cannot be a behaviour suffix on an unchanged quantizer. No earlier round used holonomy or a frame rotation.
CHANGE: For every prefix p we build a successor anchor b_p by propagating the frozen text embeddings through the row-normalised training transition matrix, and a text anchor a_p from the prefix's own items; the hyperbolic area of (origin, a_p, b_p) sets an angle theta_p, and the level's shared 256-codeword codebook is rotated by theta_p about a_p before nearest-neighbour assignment inside p. Prefixes whose items lead where they already are get theta_p = 0 and keep their baseline codes; prefixes whose successors drift away get a distinct, area-determined frame, which de-aliases the deep triples.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Notation: z_i in R^32 is the frozen Stage-1 text embedding (identical to the baseline, no trainable encoder - the variant of round one that did not collapse). Ball map psi(z) = tanh(||z||/s) * z/||z|| with s = mean_i ||z_i|| over the 24,556 items (a derived, scale-relative constant), c = 1, ball radius 1.\n(1) Behaviour matrix from the Stage-2 training split only: T[a,b] = number of consecutive pairs a->b in training histories. P(b|a) = T[a,b] / sum_b T[a,b] (zero-mass rows dropped).\n(2) For prefix p with item set S_p: a_p = psi(mean_{i in S_p} z_i); v_p(b) = (1/|S_p|) sum_{i in S_p} P(b|i); b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b). b_p lives in the SAME frozen text ball, so no cross-space projection is needed; behaviour enters only through v_p.\n(3) Poincare distance d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))). Sides: A = d(o,b_p) (opposite the angle at a_p), B = d(o,a_p), C = d(a_p,b_p).\n(4) Angles by the hyperbolic law of cosines: cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C), cyclically. Area Delta_p = max(0, pi - (alpha+beta+gamma)). Holonomy theta_p = wrap_to_(-pi,pi](-Delta_p) (Gauss-Bonnet, K = -1).\n(5) Frame at a_p: e1 = log_{a_p}(b_p)/||log_{a_p}(b_p)|| (if ||log|| < 1e-8 then theta_p := 0); u_text = top principal direction of {log_{a_p}(z_i) : i in S_p}; e2 = orthonormalise(u_text - <u_text,e1> e1). R_p is the identity except on span(e1,e2), where it is the 2x2 rotation by theta_p.\n(6) Rotated codebook for prefix p at level l: c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}( R_p log_{a_p}(c^l_k) ), k = 1..256. Assignment k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2 (ties to smallest k); residual z_i^{l+1} = log_{c'_{p,k_i}}(z_i^l) as in the baseline RQ. Level 1 uses p = root (a_p = origin), so its frame is untouched and all 256 codewords stay in play.\n(7) Stage 2 then trains the frozen recipe on reconstruction of the frozen text geometry; only decoder/residual parameters move. Frames are computed once at epoch 0 and re-checked every 100 epochs for prefix-set drift.\nPseudocode: build T; psi all z; for l in 1..3: for each active prefix p: compute a_p, v_p, b_p, Delta_p, theta_p, R_p; build c'_{p,.}; assign all items in p; update prefix sets. Then run RQ-VAE training with these fixed per-prefix codebooks."}
COST: Static pass at epoch 0 plus refresh every 100 epochs: 256 active prefixes x 3 levels, each O(32-d log/exp + a 32x32 rotation), so about 1e6 flops per pass, i.e. milliseconds. Per step the extra work is rotating the codebooks of the prefixes present in a 4096-item batch (at most ~32 prefixes x 256 codes x 32 dims = 2.6e5 flops) plus one Poincare distance matrix instead of a Euclidean one (4096 x 256 x 32 = 3.4e7 flops): expected +5 to +10% on the 0.145 s/epoch baseline, so ~0.152-0.160 s/epoch and 585-605 s for the 3000-epoch, 24-step, 4-GPU Stage 2. Stage 3 is untouched (frozen 150-epoch protocol).
HYPOTHESIS: If deep-prefix aliasing is the binding capacity problem and behaviour adds directional information only where a prefix's successors drift, then rotating just the drifting prefixes' frames should raise the number of distinct L3 triples above 2,201 and thin the items-per-triple tail, and lift Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 by giving the generator finer distinctions among the frequently queried items. Observable in distinct L3 triples, the 95th percentile of items-per-triple, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, and finally test_recall@10 / recall@5 / ndcg@10 on the frozen 57,439-query protocol.
RISKS: ['(a) A rigid per-prefix rotation can act like a relabelling: if the level-3 codebook is near rotationally symmetric the partition barely changes and triples shift without gaining information. (b) If successor drift is dominated by global popularity, v_p is nearly identical for every prefix, all theta_p cluster near one value, and the mechanism degenerates to a single global relabelling. (c) Large areas give large rotations that scatter codes arbitrarily and can hurt. (d) The 100-epoch refresh makes frames piecewise constant, so late prefix drift is only partly tracked. (e) Single run: the +/-0.003 seed noise on recall cannot be separated from a real gain.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HSPT-RQ
TITLE: Hyperbolic successor parallel-transport residual quantizer: the parent prefix's geodesic distance transports each child codebook along the item's directed-transition direction
MOTIVATION: In a generative recommender the SID is consumed as a token sequence, so what matters is whether a parent prefix (L1, L2) leaves the true next item's child prefix predictable. Round one's SID was healthy but ranking-useless: level 1 saturated 251 of 256 codewords while levels 2 and 3 collapsed to 1769 and 2201 distinct prefixes, i.e. about fourteen items share every deepest prefix and the children carry almost no discriminative information about what a user actually does next. A Euclidean RQ assigns a child codeword as if every parent prefix lived at the same place, so the child partition is blind to how far out in the hierarchy the parent already sits and to where the user's behaviour is heading from that item.
NOVELTY: The codebook is made parent-dependent by GEODESIC PARALLEL TRANSPORT, not by radial reweighting, not by Fréchet centroid updates, not by per-level curvature control, not by Gromov-delta or ancestor-depth weights, and not by cone constraints. Curvature enters as the Levi-Civita connection of the Lorentz model (transport is the identity in the flat limit), behaviour enters only as the transport DIRECTION, and they meet in a single line: the level-l codebook seen by item i is PT over the geodesic o -> P_{l-1} of C_l with direction b_i. Because transport is an isometry it cannot shrink codes toward the origin, which is the exact collapse mode that killed round one's curved residual objective.
CHANGE: Replace the level-l Euclidean nearest-codebook lookup by a lookup against a codebook that has been parallel-transported from the origin to the item's current parent prefix point, along the geodesic whose direction is the item's behaviour successor direction; the same transported vector is used for the straight-through residual, so the behaviour-and-curvature shaped partition is exactly the one the tokens encode.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Curvature fixed at K = -1 (the gauge result of issue 126 says |K| is not identifiable, so it is fixed, never tuned).\nLorentz point of tangent u in R^32: L(u) = (sqrt(1+||u||^2), u).\nexp_o(u) = L(u); log_o((x0,x)) = x.\nTransport of a spatial code vector w along the geodesic o -> P with unit spatial direction b and length rho:\n  w_par = <w,b>_E ; w_perp = w - w_par*b\n  PT(w; rho, b) = (w_par*sinh(rho), w_par*cosh(rho)*b + w_perp) in (time, space) tangent coordinates at P.\nThis is an isometry: <PT(w),PT(w)>_L = ||w||^2.\nPer item i with encoder output z (clipped, ||z||<=5) and precomputed behaviour direction b_i:\n  u <- 0 ; codes <- []\n  for l = 1..3:\n      rho <- ||u|| ; P <- L(u)\n      for k in 1..256: Q_k <- exp_{P}( PT(C_l[k]; rho, b_i) )\n      k* <- argmin_k d_L( L(z), Q_k ),  d_L((x0,x),(y0,y)) = arccosh(max(1, x0*y0 - <x,y>))\n      codes.append(k*) ; u <- u + C_l[k*]                       (straight-through: gradient copies dB/dz)\n  reconstruction loss on z_hat from the sum of C_l[k*]; commitment loss unchanged from the frozen baseline.'}
COST: Behaviour directions are precomputed once from the training split (sparse top-20 rows), so they add zero per-step cost. The extra per step is, per level, a 4096 x 256 x 33 transport plus a 4096 x 256 Lorentz distance, chunked at 512 items: about 1.0e8 elementwise ops and about 70 MB of transient memory per step at the frozen scale. Estimated 0.145 s/epoch -> 0.20-0.25 s/epoch, i.e. the 571 s Stage2 run becomes roughly 780-1050 s on the same four cards; Stage3 is untouched.
HYPOTHESIS: If parent distance and behaviour direction genuinely shape the child partition, then the number of distinct L2 and L3 prefixes must rise materially above 1769 and 2201 while level-1 usage stays broad, the measured mean transport magnitude cosh(rho) must be clearly above 1 at L3, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed the frozen 0.0679 baseline and the 0.065 gate from the single frozen run. If recall stays at 0.054 while the prefix counts rise, the mechanism is producing a finer but meaningless partition and is not worth keeping.
RISKS: ['The per-item effective codebook may become so item-specific that assignment turns arbitrary, which would raise prefix counts but destroy prefix semantics and drop recall below 0.054; deep prefixes (rho up to 5) give cosh(rho) up to 74 and can amplify the along-behaviour component until the transported codebook is dominated by b_i, so rho must be clamped and monitored; the behaviour direction derived from frozen text geometry may be too noisy for rare items (row mass below the pruning threshold), where the mechanism degenerates to identity transport.']
END IDEA
